properties.caption: Deployment: Hannibal's ~50,000 form a forward-bulging crescent -- Gallic and Spanish infantry in the centre, African veteran infantry held back on both flanks. Rome's ~60,000+ mass their heavy infantry in unusually deep ranks, citizen cavalry anchored on the river (right), allied cavalry in the open plain (left).
Skirmish: velites and Carthaginian light troops trade missiles in the gap between the lines, then fall back behind their own formations.
The crescent advances and bulges toward Rome; the Roman infantry presses forward hard into the centre. Hasdrubal's heavy cavalry charges home against the Roman citizen cavalry by the river.

Hasdrubal routs the Roman right-wing cavalry, which had no room to manoeuvre with the river at its back. The Gallic/Spanish centre begins giving ground -- the crescent starts bending concave as the Romans drive deeper into it.

The centre is now a controlled withdrawal, drawing the packed Roman ranks into a pocket. Numidian light cavalry pins the Roman allied cavalry on the far wing. Hasdrubal's cavalry, victorious by the river, rides behind the Roman line toward the Roman rear -- African veteran infantry begin wheeling inward on both flanks.
Hasdrubal's cavalry falls on the Roman allied cavalry from behind; it breaks and flees. The African veterans complete their wheel and press directly into the exposed Roman flanks.
Encirclement complete: the compressed Roman mass is surrounded on every side -- centre, both flanks, and rear -- the double envelopment that made Cannae a byword for annihilation.
